name_reason: Matches convention data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> with battle-core domain (data_fd2_battle_*) and a datatype-reflecting descriptor (counter). All evidence confirms it is the current battle turn number: init to 1 at chapter start (fd2_init_battle_state_for_chapter @ 0x2066E), +1 per completed player->NPC->enemy->player cycle (fd2_run_full_turn_cycle @ 0x1A5B9), restored from FD2.SAV +0x30C3, and rendered on-screen as decimal 'TURN N'. ~38 chapter event handlers read it for turn-gated events. No Ghidra address residue in the suffix.
purpose: Current battle turn number for the active chapter; starts at 1 and increments once per full player->NPC->enemy->player turn cycle, displayed as the on-screen 'TURN N' banner.
logic_summary: BSS zero-init uint32 scalar. Set to 1 at chapter battle init; incremented by 1 in the new-player-turn phase of fd2_run_full_turn_cycle; restored from save file (+0x30C3, 1-byte field zero-extended) on load. Read for rendering the decimal turn banner via fd2_render_decimal_number_to_buffer and by chapter turn-gated event handlers that fire cinematics/cutscenes when the turn number equals a threshold (compared as both unsigned and int32 per callsite).
element_semantics: Single 32-bit dword holding the battle turn ordinal (1-based). Stored/read as a whole dword; signed-vs-unsigned is a per-callsite cast, not a property of the storage.
notes: src/life/main.c comment block (lines 675-692) is already precise, accurate, and ASCII-only; matches all verified writers/readers, so kept unchanged. Ghidra data plate was stale/contradictory: it lived in the PRE_COMMENT field and described the symbol as 'data_fd2_save_load_save_slot_id' / save-game slot id (leftover from an earlier wrong classification, before the symbol was correctly renamed to data_fd2_battle_turn_counter). Rewrote the corrected battle-turn-counter description into the PLATE_COMMENT field (per project data-plate convention) and cleared the stale PRE_COMMENT to null. Verdict is_const=false: legitimate game writers exist (init=1, increment, save-restore). No logic/equivalence concerns found.
